blocks.title: Characters need agreed codes
blocks.text: A character set defines characters and their assigned numeric codes. An encoding specifies how those codes are represented as bytes.

blocks.title: Standard ASCII is limited
blocks.text: Seven bits provide 2⁷ = 128 codes for letters, digits, punctuation and control characters. Eight-bit extensions can provide 256 values, but different extensions may map the extra codes differently.

blocks.title: Unicode supports a much larger repertoire
blocks.text: Unicode assigns code points to characters from many writing systems and symbols. Its first 128 code points match ASCII.

blocks.title: Use the encoding stated in storage questions
blocks.text: Storage depends on the number of code points and the number of bytes used for each one. Do not assume every Unicode character uses the same width.
